the absorption of polarized light in InAs/Gas quantum dots covered by a quantum well was studied as a dependence on the intensity of the optical pump.

interband absorption spectra of InAs/Gaas quantum dots covered by a thin InGaAs quantum well have been studied experimentally and theoretically; that interband absorption cross-sections have been determined and that interband absorption can be used for light amplification.
the interband absorption spectra and the photoinduced absorption changes in InAs/Gas quantum dots covered by a InGaAs quantum well are studied.

the interband light absorption and optical amplification of the InAs/GaAS quantum dots covered by an InGaAs quantum well.

interband optical absorption and light amplification in InAs/GaNAs QDs covered by InGaAS quantum wells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interband light absorption and photoinduced changes of absorption are determined by the interband optical transitions between ground and exited quantum dot states.
Pauli blocking of the interband transitions in InAs/GaxInl-yAs/GaAs QDs is a strong function of the QD density and of the excitation intensity, but it is not a function of the dot size.
the quantum dot system under study is very well suited for the development of new types of optical devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have studied the interband light absorption and photoinduced changes of absorption in InAs quantum dots covered with InGaAs quantum well under the conditions of the interband optical pumping and have found the value of interband absorption cross-section, light amplification and Pauli blocking effect.

we have shown that the absorption cross sections in InAs/GaxIn1−xAs QDs are much larger than in bulk materials and that the interband light absorption can be used to control the absorption and amplification in QD structures.
we have studied the interband light absorption and light amplification in InAs/GaaS quantum dots covered by a thin layer of InGaAs quantum well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorption of polarized light in InAs/GaNAs QDs is not only determined by the quantum dot states, but is also affected by Pauli blocking in QDs and QWs.
we were able to measure the change of absorption under the conditions of Pauli blocking in the quantum dot system.
the interband light absorption can be used for optical control and modulation of quantum dots.
